commit_reviews.summary: Implements channel subscriptions cleanly by extending the existing ClientRegistry lock pattern and wire format, adding channel-aware routing, two new REST endpoints, and refactoring duplicated error-send logic into a helper — all backward compatible.

commit_reviews.summary: The Redis pub/sub broker and SQLite persistence follow the server's existing patterns, but every message now passes through synchronous `sqlite3` calls on the event loop, turning the async broadcast hot path into blocking I/O.

commit_reviews.summary: Cross-cutting session cleanly adds rate limiting, TTL cleanup, and a /history endpoint that mirrors the codebase's established Redis-or-local fallback, background-task lifecycle, and HTTP route conventions.

compounding_issues: Seed codebase (Flask todo app with _notify_admin stub) was entirely discarded in Session 1's greenfield rewrite; the intended incremental-carve-out never materialized, so no seed logic survived and the initial commit's constraints were moot

Dual bookkeeping of channel membership: in-memory ClientRegistry._channels is the delivery source of truth while Redis channel sets are maintained in parallel, creating a latent consistency divergence risk in multi-instance mode (e.g. /channels prefers Redis via keys() while _deliver routes locally)
Transport abstraction created in Session 4 was never exercised — TRANSPORT env only accepts 'websocket', so the seam has no second implementation validating the interface
Direct-message delivery checks recipient subscription only when a channel is present, leaving a thin authorization gap for un-channelled directs
key_decisions: Session 1 greenfield rewrite: replace the Flask seed with a purpose-built single-file async WebSocket server (notification_server.py) plus a thin app.py entry point and a real test suite
Backward-compatible channel/subscription model added in Session 2 by extending the message envelope with an optional channel field, defaulting to all-client broadcast when absent

Session 3 dual-store integration: SQLite for durable message history/pagination plus Redis pub/sub for cross-instance fan-out, with a local fast-path fallback so a single codebase degrades gracefully without Redis
Session 4 transport abstraction: extract BaseTransport/WebSocketTransport ABC to isolate all socket I/O behind an interface and delegate broadcast/send through it
Session 5 config-driven cross-cutting services: Redis-backed (with local fallback) per-minute rate limiting and message TTL cleanup/history querying controlled via env vars
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality rose monotonically across all five sessions. Session 1 established a clean, well-structured foundation (locked client registry, wire-format helpers, health endpoint, 4 passing tests). Session 2 added channels/subscriptions as a natural extension of the message envelope without breaking existing semantics. Session 3 integrated SQLite persistence and a Redis pub/sub backbone, introducing substantial but coherent complexity. Session 4 was a clean, non-destructive refactor that extracted a transport interface and re-routed I/O through it while keeping the test suite green. Session 5 layered rate limiting and message retention/history on top of the refactored core, expanding tests to 9 (8 passed, 1 skipped at HEAD). No session introduced a regression or reverted prior work; each stage widened capability and hardened structure.
story_review.summary: A textbook-coherent story where every session builds directly on the prior one, culminating in a well-architected, tested notification server whose only real debts are the unused seed and a transport abstraction waiting for its second implementation.
